# `toolu` CLI reference

Generated from the `toolu` binary by `cargo xtask docs-cli`; do not edit. `toolu <command> --help` is the reference: each page holds that output for every command beneath it, and the gate's `docs-cli` step fails when these files are stale.

- [`commands.json`](commands.json) is `toolu commands --json`, the command tree (`toolu.commands/v1`) that tools such as the Markdown drift gate (#444) read.
- [`commands.schema.json`](commands.schema.json) is `toolu commands --schema`, the JSON Schema of that tree and of every other `--json` document.
- [`installer.md`](installer.md) is the guide to `toolu plugins`, the plugin installer.

Data goes to stdout and diagnostics to stderr; with `--json`, stdout is exactly one JSON document. The exit codes are in the `toolu --help` output below. Within a major version every documented command, alias, flag, value and exit code keeps working: `cargo xtask check-cli-compat` fails a change that removes one unless `hookProtocol` is bumped in a breaking (`!`) pull request. The placeholder `planned` verbs are exempt: they go when the real verbs land.

## Hook entries

`hooks.json` calls `toolu hook <name> --event <Event> --plugin-root <dir>` for the toolu plugin and `toolu <plugin> hook <name> …` for every other plugin. Those plugin `hook` verbs are hidden from `--help`; [`hook.md`](hook.md) shows their arguments.

## `toolu --help`

```text
The one binary behind every toolu plugin's hooks, skills and commands

Usage: toolu [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  hook            Run a hook entry; hooks.json calls it (internal)
  ledger          The plan ledger, verdicts and push waivers
  debug           Count or summarize logs, stacks and failing tests
  setup           Preview, install or remove toolu's agent profiles
  doctor          Report binary, config, plugin and tool health
  config          Read, change and validate toolu.config.json
  status          Show the repository, gate and push-review status
  opencode        Run toolu plugins under OpenCode; their generated server.js calls these
  ts-quality      TypeScript quality rules that run after each edit
  python-quality  Python quality rules that run after each edit
  rust-quality    Rust quality rules that run after each edit
  ast-grep        Structural code search and rewrite with ast-grep
  brainstorm      Think a change through before building (a Markdown-only plugin)
  delivery-flow   Deliver a task end to end, from brainstorm to a babysat PR (a Markdown-only plugin)
  review          Pre-push code review state for the native push-review gate [alias: toolu-review]
  code-review     Native review of the push diff: anchored findings, coverage and a computed verdict
  docs            Inspect and record documentation reviews [alias: documentation-gate]
  jev             Typed judgments from Jev: yes/no probabilities, choices and scores
  statusline      Render and set up the native Claude status line
  babysit         Babysit a PR until CI, review threads and the review-bot verdict are clear [alias: pr-babysit]
  epic            Drive an epic to merged PRs: the resident engine, merge queue and trackers [alias: epic-orchestrator]
  sandbox         Run builds, gates and agent CLIs in a Linux sandbox: a Lima VM on macOS, this machine on Linux
  git-better      Semantic branches and commits that agents can read
  commands        List every toolu command; --json exports the tree for tools and docs
  completions     Print a bash, zsh, or fish completion script
  plugins         Install, list, remove, update and doctor toolu plugins on every host
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json
          Print exactly one JSON document on stdout

  -q, --quiet
          Drop the diagnostics of a successful run

      --host <HOST>
          The host to act for, instead of the detected one

          [possible values: claude, codex, cursor, hermes, muse, opencode]

      --config-dir <DIR>
          Read the toolu config from DIR instead of the host's default

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Output: data on stdout, diagnostics on stderr. With --json, stdout is exactly one JSON document (hooks speak their host's protocol instead).

Exit codes:
  0   success      the command did what was asked
  1   failure      the command ran and failed
  2   blocked      a hook or gate blocked or denied the action
  64  usage        the command line is wrong
  69  unavailable  a dependency (for example `gh`) is missing or unreachable
  75  tempfail     a temporary failure; the caller may retry
```
